clue.text: Raise the level, or part of it, in a duck

indicators.note: in tells us the part is placed inside the duck's name

parts.note: the scaup is a diving duck
part of it refers back to the word level, whose first two letters are taken

explanation.surface: Someone is told to raise a level, or a piece of it, while standing in a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of it' reaches back to the word 'level' just before it, so the definition's own word also lends its opening pair to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale something up is to increase it in size or degree, i.e. to raise its level.

clue.text: American cheek to name hairstyle after duck

annotationWithheld.why: American cheek to name hairstyle after duck (4): SASS is cheek, and SASS + O (duck) + ON gives SASSOON the hairstyle, but no clue word supplies ON and no parse gives every word one job
annotationWithheld.clue: American cheek to name hairstyle after duck

clue.text: Drink unknown to little 23?

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
X is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a drink is unknown to a little novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is DUMAS; the younger Alexandre Dumas (fils) could fairly be called a little Alex.
explanation.definitionFit: Alex is the short form of Alexandre, the first name of both novelist Dumases, so a diminutive for the son.

clue.text: Changed to red, angle becomes bigger

indicators.note: changed to signals the letters of the following words being remade into something else

explanation.surface: Something red alters an angle so that it grows larger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changed to' rearranges RED and ANGLE together; 'becomes' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enlarged has been made greater in size, so it is simply larger.

clue.text: Duck, one left off explorer's ship

indicators.note: off says the following letters are taken away from the duck

parts.note: the pintail is a dabbling duck
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A duck with one leg missing is aboard an explorer's vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing I (one) and L (left) from PINTAIL leaves the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pinta was one of the three vessels of Columbus's first voyage to the Americas.

clue.text: Hatched from egg, a worldwide trinket?

indicators.note: something hatched from an egg emerges in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: W and W are abbreviations for world and wide

explanation.surface: A worldwide ornament seems to have hatched out of an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram works on EGG, A and WW (world, wide).
explanation.definitionFit: A gewgaw is a showy bauble of little value, which is what a trinket is.

clue.text: Come out into considerable amount of crisis

indicators.note: a considerable amount of a word is most of it, so the last letters are dropped

parts.note: an emergency is a crisis

explanation.surface: Something comes out into a crisis of some size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'considerable amount of' keeps the first six of EMERGENCY's nine letters, dropping NCY; 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come into view or appear from a hidden place.

clue.text: Enormous duck you get turned away by Malay sahib

indicators.note: away signals the letters are sent off from the duck's name

parts.note: the garganey is a small dabbling duck

indicators.note: turned means the old word for you is read backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
tuan is the Malay word of respectful address, like sahib

explanation.surface: A huge duck is turned away by a Malay gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes EY from YE, and 'away' removes it from GARGANEY, leaving GARGAN; 'get' and 'by' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantuan, from Rabelais's giant Gargantua, means huge or colossal.

clue.text: Cooer! Duck collected nothing on podcast

indicators.note: collected means the duck gathers the other letters inside it

parts.note: the wigeon is a dabbling duck
O is nought, nothing

indicators.note: cast, as in recast, signals the word pod is rearranged

explanation.surface: A podcast in which a duck gathered nothing prompts a cry of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'podcast' is split: 'cast' is the anagram signal working on its first three letters. 'Cooer!' looks like a cry of surprise but describes a bird that coos.
explanation.definitionFit: The wood pigeon is a bird known for its soft cooing call, so it is a cooer.

clue.text: Theft of duck in grass

indicators.note: in places the duck's name inside the word for grass

parts.note: to grass is to inform, i.e. to sing to the police
the teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: Someone steals a duck that is sitting in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like a lawn, but it is the verb to inform on someone, SING.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is the act of taking another's property, which is theft.

clue.text: Odd bod with dam at party

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A strange person turns up at a party with a dam.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is an eccentric or strange person, an oddball.

clue.text: See 25
Packing up holiday home with many in 27

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
in means at home

indicators.note: in puts the letter for many inside the word for the umbrella

parts.note: the answer at 27 is a cover against rain, and a gamp is an old word for an umbrella
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

explanation.surface: A holiday home is packed up with many people inside a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: A GAMP is an umbrella, named after Mrs Gamp in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit, so 27 gives GAMP, with C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking camp means taking down tents and packing up to leave a campsite.

clue.text: Wellesley's war bears fruit, including new affront being cut short

indicators.note: including says the fruit holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: being cut short means the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: an insult is an affront

explanation.surface: In Wellington's war, fruit is borne including a fresh insult that is curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' is only a link. Wellesley is the Duke of Wellington's family name, which points to his campaign in Spain and Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Wellesley, later Duke of Wellington, led British forces in the Peninsular War against Napoleon in Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: Fight with guns for old iron

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
metal is the old naval term for a ship's guns, as in weight of metal

explanation.surface: A fight with weapons is over scrap iron.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship's guns were collectively its metal, hence weight of metal for firepower.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap metal is discarded metal such as old iron collected for recycling.

clue.text: North country fare for some churchmen at mass

indicators.note: some means only part of the word for churchmen is used, the end dropped

parts.note: ecclesiastics are churchmen, clergy
a cake is a mass, as in a cake of soap

explanation.surface: Some clergymen eat northern food at Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is a town near Manchester in the North of England; its cake is a currant pastry. 'Mass' is not the church service but a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eccles cake is a pastry from Lancashire, a classic of northern English food.

clue.text: Singer when on visit

indicators.note: on in a down clue places one word below, i.e. after, the other

parts.note: to call is to pay a visit
as can mean when

explanation.surface: A singer arrives when visiting.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'on' means placed below, so the word for 'when' comes after the word for 'visit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Callas was a famous Greek-American operatic soprano.

clue.text: It has some advantages over prison

indicators.note: some means only a part of the word advantages is taken

explanation.surface: An electronic tag has some advantages over sending someone to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'over prison' complete the surface about electronic tagging, an alternative to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Tag is the children's chasing game in which the chaser is called it.

clue.text: Piece with sure winner — love!

parts.note: con is Italian for with, familiar from musical directions
a cert is a certainty, a sure winner
O is love, nil in tennis

explanation.surface: A piece of music is described as a certain winner, with love.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a musical work for soloist and orchestra, a piece.

clue.text: Duck reported on mount

indicators.note: reported signals that the duck's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck

explanation.surface: A duck is said to be on a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech EIDER is said like IDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ida is the mountain in Crete or near Troy of Greek myth.

clue.text: Mount with woman's heart in planet, finding fruit

indicators.note: in places the other letters inside the planet's name

parts.note: Pluto was once counted the ninth planet

indicators.note: heart means the middle letters of woman

explanation.surface: A mountain and a woman's heart are found on a planet bearing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes OMA from WOMAN; MT and OMA go into PLUTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum tomato is an oval variety of tomato, and tomatoes are botanically fruit.

clue.text: Request for pupil to be put in pudding

indicators.note: to be put in says the pupil's letter goes inside the pudding

parts.note: pease pudding is a dish of boiled split peas, called pease
L is a learner, as on learner plates

explanation.surface: A pupil asks to be allowed into the pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Pease pudding is a traditional British dish of mashed split peas.
explanation.definitionFit: Please is the polite word attached to a request.

clue.text: Football manager's attendant in India eating a duck

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: eating means the attendant swallows the following letters

parts.note: a syce is a groom or stable attendant in India
the mallard is the commonest wild duck

explanation.surface: A football manager's servant in India is eating a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam Allardyce is an English football manager who briefly managed England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam Allardyce, Big Sam, has managed Bolton, Newcastle and the England team.

clue.text: Novelists form parliaments

definitions.meaning: Alexandre ... father and son were both French writers
a duma is a Russian parliament

explanation.definitionFit: The two Alexandre Dumases were novelists, and dumas are Russian legislative assemblies.

clue.text: Intriguing piece of ground

parts.note: the phrase reads both as a patch of land and as a piece of scheming

explanation.definitionFit: A plot is both a small patch of land and a secret scheme.

clue.text: Jolly good Australian misjudged if I am drunk

indicators.note: something misjudged is got wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jolly Australian got things wrong when drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misjudged' rearranges all of IF I AM DRUNK.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair dinkum is Australian slang for genuine or honest, an expression of approval.

clue.text: Deadly handicap for prince

parts.note: a let is an obstacle or hindrance, as in without let or hindrance
Hal is Prince Henry in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A deadly disadvantage hampers a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal means capable of causing death, deadly.

clue.text: Not feeling topless, to go back to France for cover

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: numb means without feeling

indicators.note: back means the French word is read in reverse

parts.note: aller is French for to go, the clue's to France signalling the language

explanation.surface: Feeling no sense of being topless, someone returns to France for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes N from NUMB; 'back' turns ALLER into RELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella gives cover from rain or sun.

clue.text: Wave that curls and flattens

definitions.meaning: a long swelling wave breaking on a shore
a hair curler sets curls, and a garden or road one flattens ground

explanation.definitionFit: A roller is a large breaking wave, a hair curler and a heavy cylinder for levelling ground.

clue.text: Love in a duck? Put your foot on it

indicators.note: in puts the letter for love inside the duck's name

parts.note: the scoter is a sea duck
O is love, nil in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone asks if there is love in a duck and is told to step on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is the tennis score nil, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A scooter is ridden by pushing one foot against the ground, so you put your foot on it.
